This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest.
SCCH-5 2.

The petition averments briefly stated as under; That on 12.12.2023 at about 9.15 a.m. petitioner was travelling in Honda Activa motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-43-Q-6180 at NH-44 Highway,
Bengaluru to Hyderabad Road, near RTO Check Post, Penukonda Town, at that time, a driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.AP-40-AF-2894 drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said motor cycle, due to the said impact, petitioner sustained severe injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Penukonda,
wherein he took first-aid, thereafter shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and then to NIMHANS Hospital, further shifted to Hosmat Hospital and then referred back to Victoria Hospital.
Petitioner has spent a sum of SCCH-5 Rs.10,00,000/- towards medical, nourishment and attendant charges.
3. At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 33 years, hale and healthy, working as Mason, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner can't do his work permanently, which resulted in loss of earnings and put to great financial hardship, untold misery and depressed.
With regard to accident crime No.231/2023 is registered against the driver of the offending vehicle before the Penukonda Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
SCCH-5 4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared before the court and filed written statement.
In the written statement respondent No.1 denied occurrence of the accident involving the alleged offending vehicle.

Further submitted that, he is owner of the Car bearing Reg.No.AP-40-AF-2894 the said car has valid fitness certificate upto 24.09.2038 and the same was insured with respondent No.2 in policy No.3001/ 208884077/00/000 valid from 25.08.2023 to 24.08.2026 and respondent No.1 had valid and effective driving licence to drive the insured car.

1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 12.12.2023 at about 9.15 a.m. near RTO Check Post,
NH-44 Highway, Bengaluru - Hyderabad Road, SCCH-5 Penukonda due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Reg. No.AP-40- AF-2894 dashed against the petitioner motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove the case, Petitioner himself examined as PW-1, examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara,
Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW-2 and marked 16 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.

On the other hand, Legal Manager of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and marked Ex.R.1.
8.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record and my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative SCCH-5 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove the case, petitioner examined himself as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1, PW-2 and documents those have marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 corroborates the case of the petitioner about occurrence of the road traffic accident dated 12.12.2023 as alleged in the petition.

R.W-1 stated that the petition filed by the petitioner is barred by limitation.
This court vide order dated 08.11.2024 condoned the delay.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, this tribunal held that the petitioner sustained the injuries due to the accident occurred on 12.12.2023 at about 9.15 a.m. when he was SCCH-5 riding Honda Activa motor cycle bearing Reg.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained fracture neck of femur left +
dislocation of head, right side midshaft radius fracture, right side 5th metacarpal fracture, L2, L3,
L4 transverse process fracture with T6 burst compression fracture.
The petitioner underwent surgery for the said injuries in the SCCH-5 form of left sided total hip Arthroplasty, ORIF with plating for right radius, CRIF with K wiring for right 5 th metacarpal.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by KIMS - Saveera Hospital wherein he took treatment as inpatient on 12.12.2023, further he took treatment as inpatient at Victoria Hospital from 13.12.2023 to 20.04.2024.

In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that,
he has not treated the petitioner and not consulted the treated Doctor prior to assessment.
Further deposed that, there are 4 fractures, left hip replacement is done, radius fracture is united, right metacarpal and T6 spine fracture is malunited.

Further deposed that, for T6 spine fracture,
petitioner has taken conservative treatment.
PW-2 deposed that, the complaints of petitioner mentioned in his affidavit are not mentioned in any previous medial records.
